leaksServices.other: {count} services the code sends data to

plan.leaksNone: The code as read sends nothing outside this computer, and nothing was seen going out in this session.
plan.leaksUnknown: unknown (the address is built at run time)
plan.leaksBrowserTitle: Called from the browser: the service sees the user's IP address and the data directly
plan.leaksNotSetTitle: Where this service keeps the data. Write it yourself in codetac.structure.json ("services": [{ "id": …, "jurisdiction": … }]); CodeTAC never fills it in.
plan.leaksNoFieldsBrowser: from the browser (field names are not recorded there)
plan.leaksOnlySeenText: These hosts received calls in this session, but the code as read does not show a call to them (an address built at run time, or a library's own call).
plan.leaksFootnote: Destinations and places come from the code as it is. Fields are names only; values are never recorded.
plan.secretsButtonTitle: Where the keys live and whether one reaches the browser
plan.secretsFootnote: Names, files and lines only: no value of a variable or key is shown, stored or sent to an AI. In code excerpts, keys written in the code are masked.
plan.secret_public_secret: {name} has a secret's name but the framework's public prefix: its value goes into the code sent to the browser.
plan.secret_secret_in_browser: {name} is a secret read in code that runs in the browser ({browser}). Without the public prefix it is empty there; with it, it would be exposed.
plan.secret_env_tracked: {files} is followed by git: its values are in the repository's history.
plan.secret_env_not_ignored: {files} is not covered by .gitignore: the next git add -A would put it in the repository.
plan.secret_env_no_git: The project is not in git and its .gitignore does not cover .env files ({files}).
plan.secret_unused: {name} is defined but no code reads it.
plan.secret_undefined: {name} is read by the code but defined in no .env file. If the hosting platform or the CI sets it, list it in codetac.structure.json ("env": { "platform": [...] }).

dataRlsCount.one: row level security on in {count} of {known}
dataRlsCount.other: row level security on in {count} of {known}

plan.dataNone: No tables found: no schema file (Prisma, Drizzle, SQL migrations, Supabase types) and no table used in the code.
plan.dataClickTable: Click a table to see who reads and writes it.
plan.dataRlsUnknown: Not known: no SQL file of the project mentions this table.
plan.dataRlsInfo: Information, not an audit: the content of the policies is not checked.
plan.dataColumnsUnknown: Columns not known: the table is known only from its use in the code.
plan.data_no_rls_browser: {name} has row level security off in the migrations and is used directly from code that runs in the browser ({browser}): anyone with the project's public key can read or change it.
plan.data_used_not_defined: {name} is used by the code, but no schema file of the project defines it.
plan.data_defined_never_used: {name} is defined, but no code of the project uses it.
plan.dataFootnote: Read from the schema files and the code as they are: tables built from a variable, and changes made only in the database's dashboard, are not seen.
plan.healthButtonTitle: Organisation problems AI-written code tends to pile up: loops, dead code, copies, shortcuts
plan.healthNone: Nothing to point out: no loops, dead files, copies or shortcuts were found.
plan.healthIntro: Information only: nothing here blocks anything. The limits are set in codetac.structure.json ("smells").
plan.healthBecauseFolder: it is in a folder that frameworks often load by themselves
plan.healthBecauseName: its name is often an entry point
plan.healthBecausePublic: it is served as it is from a public folder and may be loaded by its address
plan.smell_cycle_why: A change in one can break the other, and an AI editing one of them rarely sees the loop. It also makes them hard to move or test apart.
plan.smell_skipped_layer: {from} runs in the browser and uses {to} directly, although the project has its own server routes.
plan.smell_skipped_layer_why: Browser code that talks straight to the database or to an outside service shows its keys and logic to anyone. Going through the server routes keeps them private.
plan.smell_coupling_uses_all_why: A change anywhere can affect it: a sign that it mixes too many jobs.
plan.smell_coupling_used_by_all_why: A change there can break the whole project, so changes to it need extra care.
plan.smell_file_uses_many_why: It does too much: splitting it makes changes smaller and safer.
plan.smell_duplicate_why: A fix made in one copy is easily missed in the others. AI assistants copy code often; one shared function is easier to keep right.
plan.smell_dead_file: {file} is not imported by any file, and no framework or script starts it.
plan.smell_dead_file_possible: {file} is not imported by any file, but it may still run: {because}
plan.smell_dead_file_why: Dead code misleads you and the AI: it gets read, copied and fixed although it never runs.
plan.smell_large_file_why: Large files are hard to review, and an AI editing them tends to rewrite or cut parts it was not asked to touch.
plan.smell_unused_export: {name} in {file} is exported, but no file of the project imports it.
plan.smell_unused_export_why: It is probably left over from an earlier version; removing it makes the file easier to follow.
